title: ‘Artificial’ Filmmaker Luca Guadagnino On Whether AI Is Humanity’s Doomsday & Sam Altman’s Arsenal – Crew Call Podcast
full_text: Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping’ $120M U.S. Opening Is Second Best Start For A Prequel After ‘Rogue One’; Lionsgate Franchise Returns To Fortune – Sunday Update ‘American Psycho’ Gets Axed: Luca Guadagnino Confirms His Adaptation Is “Not Happening” ‘Artificial’ Filmmaker Luca Guadagnino On Whether AI Is Humanity’s Doomsday & Sam Altman’s Arsenal – Crew Call Podcast View All November 21, 2026 12:45pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Andrew Garfield, Monica Barbaro and Luca Guadagnino at "Artificial" Gala Screening Hara Kaur/Dave Benett/WireImage Unlike Sony’s recent theatrical release of The Social Reckoning , which arguably didn’t resonate with the current tech era we’re living in, Neon is unwrapping Luca Guadagnino ‘s Artificial about Open AI co-founders Sam Altman, Ilya Sutskever and Elon Musk at a time when we fear the technology will end us. Now whether that’s in regards to our existence or our financial livelihoods is another question. Earlier this week, former OpenAI alum and Altman rival Dario Amodei’s Anthropic went public creating a $1.18 trillion company. However, shares fell from its $111 day-of-market price to $88.91 EOD Friday. Neon is shrewdly opening Artificial limited on Christmas Day (the perfect time to launch a sophisticated adult skewing awards contender), and in the run-up to that release, following premieres at New York Film Festival and BFI London Film Fest, along with current awards voter screenings, anticipation is boiling for the pic evident in its current 95% fresh Rotten Tomatoes critics rating. Related Stories News Timothée Chalamet Addresses Possibility Of A 'Call Me by Your Name' Sequel: "Never Say Never" News Sam Altman On 'Artificial' Movie About Him -- Not Among "Ten Weirdest Things In My Life" Right Now As a filmmaker who knows something about love with the Zendaya starring tennis love triangle pic, Challengers , and Oscar winning gay romance, Call Me By Your Name, we spoke with Guadagnino on the latest Crew Call as to what pulled him into the OpenAI-verse. Watch on Deadline Take a listen below. Essentially, it’s about about a bunch of young mad, narcissistic scientists acting like flawed Greek Gods in San Francisco: Andrew Garfield as Sam Altman (center), Monica Barbaro as Mira Murati (sitting, right), and Yura Borisov as Ilya Sutskever. Well before its theatrical release, Artificial generated a lot of controversy as its original studio, Amazon MGM Studios, backed away from the movie out of fear of OpenAI. That’s because Amazon has a $50 billion investment in the Altman non-profit. However, unlike the Facebook camp back when Social Network was getting released in 2010, there’s been zero ill will coming from Altman or OpenAI about Guadaganino’s film. In fact, you could say they’re great sports. In a sit-down with the Vanity Fair podcast, Altman says he “did not” coerce Amazon to drop Artificial. “I don’t know anyone else who did,” he added, “I didn’t speak to Jeff Bezos.” In fact, Guadagnino brazenly shot the pic outside Altman’s house in San Francisco. The filmmaker tells us about that. For Altman, he was giddy about running into his onscreen doppelgänger, Andrew Garfield: “One morning, I was walking down the street to get coffee and there were all these cameras and there was a guy dressed exactly like me with the same backpack, walking so much, I felt like I was in a weird glitch or a simulation.” Altman emphasized to Vanity Fair that Garfield “did walk like me.” While Altman hasn’t seen Artificial, his reaction to the trailer is, “I don’t think they’re going for accuracy, so in that sense it doesn’t bother me. They’re trying to make a good movie and maybe it will be good. It won’t be good as an accurate depiction, except for the walk. I’m sure they’ll get other parts right at least accidentally.” One of the jaw dropping moments shown in the Artificial trailer is Altman having a bunker in his wine country estate loaded with guns. “That is an example of an inaccuracy,” Altman told Vanity Fair, “There’s no bunker with firearms on the wall.” “I have a survivalist mindset,” Altman admitted, “but I don’t have a setup that is depicted in that trailer.” Guadagnino tells Deadline, “I have validated the validating information that has been vetted: He does have guns.” While the filmmaker experienced zero pushback from OpenAI and Altman during production on the Simon Rich script, he says “We were very careful that everything that was in the movie had to be approved legally, so that we were not bending facts and reality for our narrative purposes. But, because the truth in this case is more extraordinary than any fiction, that was okay. Because we had the drama, we had the juice.” When it came to Amazon exiting Artificial , Guadagnino had a Zen mindset: “I was cool because I like disruptions, very much.” “Their decision to give the movie to us to find another home was truly honorable, because they could have written off the movie and (said) ‘Bye-bye’.” As far as Artificial being a hot potato that no studio wanted to handle, except NEON, Guadagnino asserts that “All the speculation about nobody wanting the movie; I like to think that there was the need (by the media) to fill blank pages with nothing.” For off the bat, per Guadagnino, NEON was first, front and center in their passion to takeover the project after CAA screened it for them. Listen above for more details. When it comes to the paranoia out there that AI is the catalyst for human extinction in ten years, the filmmaker tells Deadline, “I don’t have trust and I don’t have faith in humans.” His suspicions about AI stem from growing up during the Cold War. “I remember very well in 1985 when Chernobyl happened,” he adds. And there’s myriad reasons for concerns about AI, from a Chatbot being at the center of 16-year old Adam Raine’s suicide , to AI trespassing and impostering another company’s security space We also talk with the Call Me By Your Name Best Picture Oscar nominee on why Andrew Garfield was the right guy to play Altman, and the Open AI Boss’ sincerity when it comes to creating guardrails for the technology. ‘Sunrise On The Reaping’ Opens To $120M NA; Franchise Returns To Fortune ‘Home Alone’ Sequel With Macaulay Culkin In Early Works From Rogen & Goldberg Big Stars Coming To Heat Up Broadway’s Winter ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ Speeds Aways With Nearly $4 Billion In Day 1 Sales Read More About: Comments

title: How Raising Cane’s Became an A-List Magnet
full_text: × Skip to main content By Kirsten Chuba Plus Icon Kirsten Chuba Events Editor kirstenchuba Follow Sign Up View All November 21, 2026 10:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Teyana Taylor makes a Cane’s run after winning a Golden Globe this year. Courtesy of Raising Cane’s There’s a new billionaire in town — and this one’s ready to party. Todd Graves, founder and CEO of chicken fingers chain Raising Cane’s, has quickly gained a reputation for hosting Hollywood’s hottest events, splashing out for A-list gatherings around major sporting events and awards shows. During last summer’s World Cup, the 54-year-old Louisiana native rented out stadium suites nationwide, throwing parties with guests including Woody Harrelson , Sacha Baron Cohen, Mick Jagger, Halle Berry , Jamie Foxx, Ashton Kutcher, Adam Brody, Florence Pugh, Alix Earle , Tate McRae and Matt Damon (during opening weekend of The Odyssey , no less). He also enlisted Tiffany Haddish to serve chicken fingers and host Raising Cane’s-branded interviews backstage at the Emmys, persuaded Adrien Brody to paint a custom mural for his Times Square store and is getting the biggest winners across sports and awards season to come by his restaurants immediately after their victories, establishing a tradition to rival the post-awards In-N-Out run. Related Stories Beyond the Book "The Secrecy Was Insane:" The Making of 'The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping,' From Locked Safes to Original Cast's Return Movies Teyana Taylor Sells Female-Driven Comedy to Warner Bros. (Exclusive) How exactly did a brand serving $15 chicken finger meals — whose nearest competitor is Chick-fil-A — become such a popular collab magnet for the rich and famous? Graves says the secret sauce is his own up-by-the-bootstraps backstory, which he sees as the ultimate icebreaker: Having worked as a boilermaker in California oil refineries and as a salmon fisherman as a young man, he went on to launch his fast food empire — which 30 years later, according to Forbes , has landed him a net worth of $20 billion. Halle Berry and Jamie Foxx at a party for the USA-Paraguay World Cup game hosted by Graves at SoFi Stadium in June. Phillip Faraone/Getty Images Graves says he does not pay celebrities to attend his events but instead provides a high-end, all-inclusive outing. “I want it to be like, ‘I want to go hang out with Todd and go to this event.’ It’s first-class, great hotels, transportation, security,” Graves says of his pitch. “No one in there wants anything from them but friendship, hanging out.” He adds that on top of the fact that “the dinners are great, the parties are fun, there’s DJs and performers that they like,” it’s important to him to take out the corporate element, with no business partners in his rooms “hitting people up or asking for selfies.” From left: Raising Cane’s founder and CEO Todd Graves, Rob Gronkowski in a Cane’s sauce dunk tank and Tom Brady in July. Phillip Faraone/Getty Images There is a catch: Graves does ask his guests to post on their social media channels, telling them up front that ” ‘It helps me get a return on this and we can keep doing great events,’ and they’re all cool about doing that.” Haddish and Snoop Dogg have been particularly enthusiastic posters for the brand, while on the Raising Cane’s channel, Tom Brady declared its Fanatics Fest event (which featured a dunk tank of Cane’s sauce) “my favorite part of the entire week.” Graves confirms that the company measures impressions after every event, and “it’s amazing for sales,” he adds. “You see long-term loyalty because [customers] are like, ‘The person that I really love and respect loves Cane’s and actually wants to hang out with the founder.’ “ Raising Cane’s fan Adrien Brody shows off his art at a New York event for the brand. Courtesy of Raising Cane’s The CEO, who this year bought a home in the Hollywood Hills for a reported $23 million, says he doesn’t do cold calls to invite people he doesn’t know. “It looks like a branded thing,” he says, which, to be fair, it very much is, judging by the ubiquity of the chain’s logo in celebrities’ posts. Instead, he fills his events with stars with whom he is friendly. That helps him expand the Hollywood circle in a more organic way, through word-of-mouth. Damon, for instance, came to the Raising Cane’s World Cup celebrations because Casey Affleck, a friend of Graves’, vouched that the events were good. Graves’ friend group also includes Adrien Brody — who showed off his artwork while Graves was hanging out at the actor’s home, leading to the idea to paint a custom piece for the New York store — and Teyana Taylor , who dropped by a Cane’s for a photo op after winning at the Golden Globes earlier this year. “We want to be part of culture when it happens,” he says, having organized the plan with Taylor before the awards show, getting her to come by before her night of parties. (These photo moments are executed as more traditional brand deals.) 50 Cent performs at a Raising Cane’s event in New York City. Phillip Faraone/Getty Images The Raising Cane’s founder says he was on the road 260 days in 2025, and he doesn’t seem to be slowing down as the brand expands into Europe and begins to plan international events. (Baron Cohen is helping connect him to contacts in London, Graves says.) He also notes that despite his connections and financial status, he doesn’t have any aspirations to produce projects or be actively involved in Hollywood — though he does think another friend, Leonardo DiCaprio, should play him in the story of his life. But L.A. remains as much of a home base as Louisiana. “The town has so accepted me. [It’s] so diverse, so rich culturally. I love it,” Graves says. “So for me, [the goal] is just to keep meeting these great people. L.A. is so full of all these amazing people that I get inspired by.” Tiffany Haddish and Matthew Rhys backstage at the Emmys. Courtesy of Raising Cane’s This story appeared in the Nov. 18 issue of The Hollywood Reporter magazine.

title: Lindsay Hubbard Teases ‘Summer House’ Spinoff ‘In the City’ Season 2: “Better Than Season One”
full_text: Skip to main content By Lexi Carson Plus Icon Lexi Carson Associate Editor View All November 21, 2026 8:15am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Lindsay Hubbard Charles Sykes/Bravo via Getty Images Logo text Amid filming season two of Bravo ‘s In the City , being a mom and her charitable efforts, Lindsay Hubbard is having a busy fall. Hubbard’s latest venture is partnering with No Kid Hungry’s Amplify Impact campaign ahead of Thanksgiving. The reality star served free breakfast sandwiches to New Yorkers at Give Back Bodega alongside season 21 Top Chef winner Danny Garcia at a pop-up event in Manhattan earlier this week. The campaign aims to help 10 million more kids access meals by 2032. “One in five kids faces hunger every day in the United States, and as a kid, they should just be kids. They should be playing and having a good time, and they shouldn’t have to think about where their next meal is coming from,” she told The Hollywood Reporter . Related Stories TV Melania Trump Stresses Humanitarian Efforts at Chic Premiere for Two-Episode Series Documentary Follow-Up Movies 'I Play Rocky' Stars Unite With Original 'Rocky' Producer for Film's 50th Anniversary Celebration The cause has taken on an even greater significance for Hubbard as a mother. Her daughter, Gemma Britt Kufe, turns two next month, and she explained how motherhood has changed her perspective on childhood hunger. “When I’m with Gemma, I have no nannies. I’m single mom-ing it hard,” she said. “I am spending my days feeding her, caring for her, making sure she’s eating. That’s the one thing that I’m always constantly thinking about. Courtesy of Give Back Bodega Hubbard’s transition into motherhood has also been documented on Bravo’s Summer House and its spinoff, In the City , which was recently renewed for a second season . While she remained tight-lipped about the upcoming season because the show is currently in production, she teased that fans will be satisfied with what’s to come. “We’re in the middle of filming it right now, and let me tell you, it’s got all of the elements of a great season two, better than season one,” Hubbard said. Page Six reported in October that the sophomore season will feature a cast shake-up. According to the outlet, new castmembers include Brittany Whitfield, Robert Morrison, Reagan Baker, Natasha Parker and Barthelemy Jallet. Meanwhile, season one stars Amanda Batula, Danielle Olivera and her partner, Eoin Heavey, as well as Andrea Denver and his wife, Lexi Sundin, will not be returning. Batula’s departure comes amid a particularly eventful period for the Summer House cast. She also exited ahead of season 11 of the original series amid the controversy surrounding her relationship with co-star West Wilson, who previously dated her close friend and fellow castmember Ciara Miller. Batula and her husband, OG Summer House star Kyle Cooke , had separated before the reports surfaced. Cooke was also close friends with Wilson. In alleged Instagram DMs, Batula cited intense online “hate” and “bullying” over her relationship with Wilson as her reason for not returning. Bravo has yet to officially announce the cast for In the City season two and did not respond to THR’s request for comment. Meanwhile, Hubbard herself has made headlines amid filming for the upcoming season. Earlier this month, Page Six reported that Cooke made out with Hubbard over Halloween weekend while filming a cast trip in Cancun, Mexico. The pair have been friends for more than a decade, and Cooke is also best friends with Carl Radke, Hubbard’s ex-fiancé and another OG Summer House castmember. Hubbard addressed the speculation with a laugh, telling THR, “No, Kyle’s like a brother to me. We just have a lot of fun, you know.” From left: Carl Radke, Hubbard and Kyle Cooke at Bravo Fan Fest in Charleston, South Carolina, on Oct. 24, 2026. Jessica Yurinko/Bravo via Getty Images With Summer House season 11 and In the City season two on the horizon, Hubbard isn’t expecting to step away from reality television anytime soon. “I’ll do it as long as they’ll have me on all these shows. I live a really big, full life that rarely ever stops. Things happen, and I have a lot to share at all times,” she said. “So until that stops, then maybe the TV portion would stop for me, but I don’t see that stopping anytime soon.” Also forthcoming is Hubbard’s memoir, Activated , which will be released May 18. Despite spending a decade on television, she said she still has plenty of stories she hasn’t shared with audiences. “I don’t need to rehash things that you can go back and rewatch,” she said of what readers can expect from the book. “So it’s all the stories that happen in life. I turned 40 this year, so you haven’t seen the first 30 years of my life. This is childhood, high school, college, my early PR days in New York, me living in L.A., me coming back to New York.” Hubbard added that she’s “actually really nervous” about readers discovering some of those previously untold stories. “I have been giggling and crying. It’s a lot of vulnerability,” she said. “I’m actually really nervous to open up some of these stories that people have never heard before, and it’s also the wildest moments of my entire life. There’s no holding back.” THR

title: NBC to Air Princess of Wales Cancer Charity Documentary
full_text: Skip to main content By Rick Porter Plus Icon Rick Porter Television Business Editor rickporter Follow Sign Up View All November 21, 2026 4:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Catherine, Princess of Wales Jordan Pettitt - Pool/Getty Images Logo text NBC will air a documentary special following the Princess of Wales as she completes a charity challenge to raise money for cancer patients. Heal: A Princess of Wales Special is set to air at 8 p.m. ET/PT Nov. 30 on NBC, a day after it premieres on the BBC in the U.K. The special will also at 11:30 p.m. Nov. 30 on Bravo and stream on Peacock starting Dec. 1. Heal will explore “life beyond diagnosis and the many ways people find comfort, strength and hope in the face of serious illness,” a description reads. Cameras followed Catherine as she completed the Three Peaks Challenge — climbing the tallest mountains in England, Scotland and Wales in the course of 24 hours — in June in support of the Royal Marsden Cancer Charity. It will also feature the stories of other people facing cancer (the princess was diagnosed with a form of cancer in 2024 but was in remission as of 2025). “[Cancer] changes your body, it changes you physically,” Catherine says in a trailer for the special (watch it below). “But there’s a much, much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you.” All money from distribution of the special (it will also air in Australia on Dec. 1 and Canada on Dec. 7) will go to the Royal Marsden Cancer Charity to help people living with and after a cancer diagnosis. Detail Films produced the special, with Benji Jackson directing. THR

title: Netflix’s ‘Minimum Wage’ Ushers In Streaming’s Short Ep Sitcom Era: “The Future Is 15-Minute ‘SpongeBob’-Length Episodes”
full_text: Skip to main content By Peter White Peter White Executive Editor, Television @peterzwhite More Stories By Peter Netflix’s ‘Minimum Wage’ Ushers In Streaming’s Short Ep Sitcom Era: “The Future Is 15-Minute ‘SpongeBob’-Length Episodes” Lauren Neustadter Exiting Reese Witherspoon’s Hello Sunshine Nat Geo Explores The Unabomber’s Brother, Somali Pirates & Hantavirus In New Doc Slate View All November 21, 2026 11:06am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Minimum Wage Netflix In a world of increasingly short attention spans, social media slop and doomscrolling brainrot, it’s a wonder why many television shows got longer in the streaming era. Case in point, the 22-minute broadcast sitcom was largely replaced by the 30-minute dramedy and the 43-minute procedural has been overshadowed by the hour-long premium drama series. Netflix , however, has found success with a much shorter concept in Minimum Wage . The comedy series, which comes from Jeremy Garelick and Will Phelps’ American High , consists of 14 episodes between 12 and 20 minutes in its first tranche, which debuted at the end of October. Related Stories Podcast American High Levels Up: How Jeremy Garelick & Will Phelps Are Scaling Unconventional Comedy Company – Comedy Means Business Podcast News ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’: Here Is Why Episodes Of ‘Big Bang Theory’ Spinoff Are So Short Set in a pizza joint and starring new SNL darling Grace Reiter , Aidan Micho, Hyde Healy, Julia Dicesare, Luke Burke, Ryan Micho, Tommy Armstrong and Randall Park, its short episodes are a feature, not a bug. Watch on Deadline Phelps told Deadline, “The future is these 15-minute kind of SpongeBob -length episodes where it’s really fast. There’s not any fat.” In fact, Netflix demanded short episodes for the show, which began life as a series of YouTube sketches shot during the middle of the night with interns as camera operators and a building manager handling the boom mic. Garelick said, “When we closed the deal, [Netflix] said that they wanted it to be a minimum of twelve and a half-minute episodes. It was an interesting challenge because most episodic TV shows are 22 to 30 pages. It was almost like we were inventing a new structure as we were going and it was hard.” Episodes were also capped at 20 minutes with shooting scripts ending up being around 15 pages and the cast encouraged to improv. “You can captivate an audience for 15 minutes really well,” Phelps added. “Jeremy and I are coming at it from traditional screenplay writing and the cast is coming at it from making the most exciting one-minute thing for TikTok or Instagram.” This contrast is both the essence of Minimum Wage and also highlights one of the industry’s challenges as creators such as Druski and others are increasingly working on scripted projects for streamers. “Everyone’s clamoring for creators to make shows now [following] the success of Obsession and Minimum Wage and I’m nervous that without the guidance of traditional screenwriters, you might fall into a trap of creators that are used to taking a one-minute premise and being told expand that into 15 minutes. That’s just going to be full of fat. Whereas we’re taking stories that really should be a half-hour and squeezing the fat out from the other side. That’s the secret sauce that we have.” Minimum Wage (Netflix) Garelick began his career working as an assistant for Joel Schumacher and working on movies such as The Break-Up and The Wedding Ringer before teaming up with Phelps to buy a high school in upstate New York, where they made films such as Banana Split, Holly Slept Over and Pete Davidson-starrer Big Time Adolescence. “We’ve become a traditional Hollywood studio, but we give a lot more trust to the creators and the artists, and we have an academy, our shorts and our sketch teams, and we’re kind of combining [it all],” said Garelick. This also allowed American High to deliver more episodes of Minimum Wage than Netflix had originally ordered. The streamer initially greenlit 20 episodes but they ended up writing 28 scripts and persuaded Netflix that it would be cheaper to produce them all. “We don’t get hung up on the actual business side of things. We’ll just do it for the love of the game,” added Phelps. Minimum Wage debuted last month and reached Netflix’s global top ten charts with 2.4M views, impressive given the season’s run time is under four hours. It is one of a number of streaming shows keeping episode lengths concise. Shane Gillis’ Netflix comedy series Tires is generally in the 20-23-minute range, while HBO Max’s The Big Bang Theory spinoff Stuart Fails To Save The Universe consists of episodes between 18 and 20 minutes with one episode clocking in at only 15 minutes. Stuart Fails To Save The Universe Colin Remas Brown/HBO Max Co-creator Chuck Lorre, who has spent the vast majority of his career working in broadcast comedy, said there was “no real reason” to pad the episodes . “The historic length of a show is entirely arbitrary, it comes from network television where a certain amount of advertising has to be sold to pay the way of making this television, but it’s not an element any longer in streaming,” Lorre said. “So, why not just make the best show we can and hope the audience is entertained and is not looking at their watch.” Minimum Wage works because it is a workplace comedy, one featuring an overwhelmed group of teenagers struggling to run The Slice Club, where the “stakes are low and the pressure is immense.” It’s not clear whether the remaining 14 episodes that American High shot will be labeled as the second part of season one or season two, but they are expected to air in spring 2027. There’s also plenty of road for more episodes; Garelick said that they’ve already got around 50 more draft scripts. The pair are also developing more projects using a similar model of testing out ideas across its YouTube channels including American High Shorts, which has over 4.5M subscribers, College Life, which has over 1M subs, and Entry Level and Gurgle, USA. “It takes a few months to get there, and then it takes a year or so of incubating that online to get a fan base, and then you’re ready to start a show with some solid footing behind it, and the audience feels like they were part of the inception of this,” said Phelps. “I think it’s the future of TV.” ‘Sunrise On The Reaping’ Opens To $120M NA; Franchise Returns To Fortune Netflix’s ‘Minimum Wage’ Ushers In Streaming’s Short Ep Sitcom Era Big Stars Coming To Heat Up Broadway’s Winter ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ Speeds Aways With Nearly $4 Billion In Day 1 Sales Read More About: 2 Comments

title: Broadway’s Cure For The Post-Holiday Blues? Stars, Stars & More Stars, Coming This Winter
full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg CAA’s Bryan Lourd Urges Congress To Pass AI Legislation To Protect Americans “Famous Or Not” Broadway’s Cure For The Post-Holiday Blues? Stars, Stars & More Stars, Coming This Winter Lincoln Center Theater Names Naomi Weinstock New Executive Director Of Development; Robert Jones Upped View All November 21, 2026 11:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Julia Roberts, Steve Carell, Jonathan Groff Getty/Robert Ascroft/Chad Meyer With Thanksgiving almost here, it’s not too early for Broadway to start thinking about…March? In case you’ve noticed a lot of big, starry announcements in recent weeks for shows that will open this spring – and not just spring proper like the Tony-heavy month of April, but the chillier weeks just after the December holidays but before the Easter thaw. Why announce now? The better to entice potential ticket-buyers into surprising their beloveds with gift-wrapped tickets (or printed payment confirmations) to see Julia Roberts , Paul Rudd and Sarah Paulson this early March, or Steve Carell and John C. Reilly a week or two later. Merry Christmas, Happy Hanukkah and Happy Easter all rolled into one. Related Stories News 'Much Ado About Nothing' Broadway Review: Tom Hiddleston, Hayley Atwell & Jamie Lloyd Throw An Irresistible Party Of Shakespeare's Great Comedy News Josh Radnor & Beth Behrs To Join Broadway's 'Schmigadoon!' Broadway’s upcoming winter season comes as a very star-packed fall is raking up strong weekly grosses. Last week, the critically-blessed Much Ado About Nothing starring Tom Hiddleston and Hayley Atwell grossed a whopping $2,352,287, while Crystal’s 860 broke the house record for a play at the Imperial Theatre with a big $1,720,253. Other Desert Cities , starring Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Ed Harris, Allison Janney, Joe Keery and Lily Rabe, grossed $2,570,589, a common enough occurrence for that show to place it week after week alongside such a $2M+ stalwart as Hamilton . Watch on Deadline But Broadway won’t be resting on its pine-scented laurels for long: A week after the holidays, Manhattan Theatre Club’s Awake and Sing! revival starring West Wing ‘s Richard Schiff, Jessica Hecht, Will Pullen, Danny Burstein and others opens January 7 (previews start December 15), and in short order the much anticipated Dolly: A True Original Musical (St. James Theatre) opens January 19 (previews start December 7) and Mix and Master, the Dominique Morisseau play starring Ruben Santiago-Hudson and Kara Young, begins previews January 5 at the Todd Haimes Theatre ahead of an opening night on January 27, 2027. The March openings begin with Three Days of Rain , the Broadway revival of Richard Greenberg’s Pulitizer-finalist play with a big-name cast of François Arnaud, David Corenswet and Yvonne Strahovski. Performances begin Saturday, January 30, 2027, at the Longacre Theatre, with a March 1 opening night. It’s a 16-week engagement. The Amish Project starring Jonathan Groff is a one-person play written Jessica Dickey, directed by Sarna Lapine, about an Amish community coming together in the wake of tragedy. Previews begin at the Broadhurst Theatre on February 10 ahead of an early March opening. The starry month continues with Small Mouth Sounds , and, at least in terms of celebrity names, is the winter show to beat: Julia Roberts, Paul Rudd and Sarah Paulson lead the cast of Bess Wohl’s play that also includes Martin Freeman, Greta Lee and Isaac Powell. Joe Mantello directs, with Scott Rudin and Barry Diller producing. Previews begin February 10 at the Ethel Barrymore Theater, with an opening on March 11. Next comes Dirty Dancing The Musical, starring Annalese Starzec and Blake Zelesnikar, both Broadway newcomers, but no matter: The star power of this one is the title itself, a name certain to stir nostalgia for fans of the Jennifer Grey and Patrick Swayze classic film romance. The new stage production based on the 1987 film will arrive on Broadway this winter for a limited seven-month engagement. Performances begin Friday, February 12, 2027, at Broadway’s Lena Horne Theatre with a “gala celebration” on Sunday, March 14. Birthright , beginning previews February 23 at the Hudson ahead of a March 15 opening, carries the imprimatur of a very successful and acclaimed Off Broadway run last summer, along with the reputation of the playwright – Jonathan Spector – who scored a major Broadway success last year with the Tony-winning Eureka Day . Casting for the play hasn’t been announced, but the Off Broadway production starred such New York stage favorites as Molly Ranson, Nate Mann, Liz Larsen, Eli Gelb, Molly Bernard, Zoë Winters and Hale Appleman. March’s final weeks will continue the celebrity appeal with The Odd Couple , starring Steve Carell, who will play the persnickety Felix Ungar, and John C. Reilly, as the slob Oscar Madison. Hamilton ‘s Thomas Kail directs at the Stephen Sondheim Theatre, with performances for the 15-week engagement beginning March 3, 2027, and an opening on March 23. And March goes out like a lion with Evita , director Jamie Lloyd’s revival of the Tim Rice and Andrew Lloyd Webber musical starring Rachel Zegler reprising her Olivier Award-winning performance as Eva Perón. Previews start February 27 at the Winter Garden – currently the home of Lloyd’s magnificent Much Ado – with an opening night of March 25. Evita will be the final opening before the spring crunch of Tony-qualifying last minute arrivals goes full swing, and, yes, those shows will have plenty of stars as well – Jessica Chastain, Bryan Cranston, Laura Linney, Neil Patrick Harris and more. Those April openers include Gloria (April 5), Warriors (April 8), Purple Rain (April 12), All My Sons (April 13), The Sound of Music (April 15), Paddington The Musical (April 18), Montauk (April 19), Damn Yankees (April 20), Lost Lear (April 23) and Rhinoceros (April 25). ‘Home Alone’ Sequel With Macaulay Culkin In Early Works From Rogen & Goldberg Big Stars Coming To Heat Up Broadway’s Winter ‘Sunrise On The Reaping’ Eyeing $120M-Plus Domestic Bow ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ Speeds Aways With Nearly $4 Billion In Day 1 Sales Read More About: Comments

title: CAA’s Bryan Lourd Urges Congress To Pass AI Legislation To Protect Americans “Famous Or Not”
full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg CAA’s Bryan Lourd Urges Congress To Pass AI Legislation To Protect Americans “Famous Or Not” Broadway’s Cure For The Post-Holiday Blues? Stars, Stars & More Stars, Coming This Winter Lincoln Center Theater Names Naomi Weinstock New Executive Director Of Development; Robert Jones Upped View All November 21, 2026 11:34am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Bryan Lourd John Salangsang/Getty Images CAA chief Bryan Lourd is urging the full Congress to pass the No Fakes Act and deliver it to President Trump for signature, a move Lourd says would protect everyone, famous or not, from nonconsensual digital replicas of their voices and likenesses. Related Stories Agencies CAA’s Bryan Lourd Insists AI’s “Future Must Be Built With Artists, Not At Their Expense” As Agency Weighs In On NYT Vs. OpenAI Battle News Tech Stocks End Dismal Week On Harsh Note; Nasdaq Slides Another 5% And Is Now Flat For The Year In a guest essay published in today’s New York Times, Lourd writes, “The Senate and House should move quickly and deliver the bill to President Trump for signature. That would ensure Americans retain control of their images and voices in the A.I. era.” The No Fakes Act was approved unanimously by the Senate Judiciary Committee in June, and, Lourd contends, there “is momentum to pass it through the full Congress before the end of the year.” He calles it “one of the few A.I. bills with true bipartisan support.” Watch on Deadline Hollywood, Lourd writes, “is not afraid of new technology.” “The objection from actors, musicians and other creators is to a world in which anyone can use their face or voice without permission,” he writes. “In fact, many artists are already embracing A.I. on their own terms. Some of them are making deals with companies that are creating their A.I. likenesses, with their consent.” Lourd poses the issue as not just for Hollywood. “A content creator learned on her honeymoon that a YouTube ad was using an A.I. version of her to sell erectile dysfunction supplements,” he writes. “Is all this legal? Right now, it’s an open question. But it shouldn’t be.” “Hollywood doesn’t need America’s leaders to devise a new concept for new circumstances,” writes the chief executive and co-chairman of Creative Artists Agency. “We need them to extend and enforce the rules that already exist. The use of Americans’ faces, voices, performances and creative works is already subject to rules at the federal or state level that say, in short: You need to get permission, and you need to pay for the use.” “This principle has guided the entertainment industry for more than a century,” he continues. “Whether it can continue to protect Americans may be decided in the coming weeks. The No Fakes Act would create a federal prohibition on creating nonconsensual digital replicas of any person’s voice or likeness — famous or not.” The No Fakes Act, Lourd says, “would apply a tried-and-true formula to the A.I. era: control, consent and compensation. It would set a uniform federal standard to replace outdated, ill-fitting state laws, many of them written with an analog world in mind. Its supporters include all sides of the table: SAG-AFTRA, the union representing actors and other performers; the Motion Picture Association, representing the studios; and tech companies including IBM, Google and OpenAI.” Earlier this month, Lourd told Deadline’s Dominic Patten, that the issues around AI are “about the fundamental relationship between technological progress and creative rights, and who determines the value of creative work, who decides how that work is used, and whether creators will share in the opportunities AI creates.” Read Deadline’s exclusive interview with Lourd here . ‘Sunrise On The Reaping’ Opens To $120M NA; Franchise Returns To Fortune Netflix’s ‘Minimum Wage’ Ushers In Streaming’s Short Ep Sitcom Era Big Stars Coming To Heat Up Broadway’s Winter ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ Speeds Aways With Nearly $4 Billion In Day 1 Sales Read More About: 1 Comments

title: Watermelon Expands Production Ambitions As It Seals Partnership With Qatar’s Film Committee
full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Egyptian Music Star Mohamed Mounir Gets Biopic – Doha Industry Days ‘Al Hayba’ Star Taim Hasan To Play Syrian Whistleblower Farid Al-Madhhan In Neon-Backed ‘Caesar’ Biopic Steven Paul Talks Up Federal Film & TV Tax Credit: “It’s Going To Be Good For The World” – Industry Days Doha View All November 21, 2026 11:43am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Badie Ali, Hassan Al-Thawadi, Hamza Ali Film Committee at Media City Qatar Watermelon Pictures and the Film Committee at Media City Qatar have announced a planned strategic partnership to develop and co-produce a slate of films telling stories from the Global South. The partnership marks a significant expansion into larger-scale, mainstream production for Watermelon Pictures. Badie Ali and Hamza Ali launched their Chicago-based production and distribution company in 2024, with a mission to amplify Palestinian and other under-represented voices. Until now, the company has focused mainly on distribution, with recent releases including The Voice of Hind Rajab , El Sett , Who Killed Alex Odeh? and American Doctor . Related Stories News Egyptian Music Star Mohamed Mounir Gets Biopic - Doha Industry Days News 'Al Hayba' Star Taim Hasan To Play Syrian Whistleblower Farid Al-Madhhan In Neon-Backed 'Caesar' Biopic Its cofounders recently signaled to Deadline that they were working on a development slate , without going into detail. Watch on Deadline The strategic partnership aims to combine Qatar ’s infrastructure and resources as it seeks to grow the film and TV sector at home and regionally, and Watermelon’s access to leading talent, established distribution infrastructure, and understanding of what resonates with audiences. “When we founded Watermelon Pictures, our vision was to bring powerful stories to the big screen with an unwavering commitment to authenticity,” said Watermelon Pictures cofounder Badie Ali. “Our partnership with the Film Committee at Media City Qatar is a major step toward realizing that promise, allowing us to tell these stories on a larger scale while remaining true to the people and places at their heart.” Under the partnership, the parties would aim to shoot projects substantially in Qatar or structure them as Qatari co-productions. They would also seek to involve Doha-based post-production companies and help eligible projects access the Qatar Screen Production Incentive (QSPI), creating opportunities for local crews, businesses, and creative talent while strengthening Qatar’s position as an international production hub. “Through this partnership, we want to give filmmakers the resources to tell stories rooted in their communities and bring them to audiences around the world. We also want the films we support to create work for crews and businesses in Qatar and give them experience they can carry into their next production,” said Hassan Al Thawadi, Chairman of the Film Committee at Media City Qatar. The Film Committee and Watermelon Pictures will jointly identify projects for the initial slate. The proposed partnership is subject to definitive agreements and the required approvals, with projects to be considered individually. More details on specific projects are soon to be announced “ Too many compelling stories and perspectives, including those of Arab and Muslim communities, have historically been underrepresented in mainstream cinema. We see an enormous opportunity to change that. Our planned slate will span genres, challenge perceptions, and, above all, entertain. Our ambition isn’t simply to create space in the industry. It’s to compete at its highest level,” said Watermelon Pictures cofounder Hamza Ali. The announcement of the planned partnership was made during the Film Committee’s Doha Industry Days, running from November 19 to 21 within the framework of the Doha Film Festival . ‘Sunrise On The Reaping’ Opens To $120M NA; Franchise Returns To Fortune ‘Home Alone’ Sequel With Macaulay Culkin In Early Works From Rogen & Goldberg Big Stars Coming To Heat Up Broadway’s Winter ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ Speeds Aways With Nearly $4 Billion In Day 1 Sales Read More About: Comments

full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Sean Astin Mobilizes SAG-AFTRA In Fight For Universal Healthcare As “Substantial Majority” Of Members Don’t Qualify For Insurance ‘Yellowjackets’ Creators On Ending Show Ahead Of Original Five-Season Plan: “We Chose To Try To Squeeze It In” John Carpenter Reveals Robert Rodriguez Back In Running To Helm ‘Escape from New York’ Reimagining View All November 20, 2026 8:17pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Bill Maher comments on 'GTA VI' and Robert Pattinson's casting as James Bond.
